exposure: Intimate partner violence (before or during pregnancy)
Number of psychosocial stressors (around pregnancy or birth)
outcome: Effectiveness level of postpartum contraceptive method used (none, less effective, moderately effective, long-acting reversible contraception, or sterilization)
cohort: The study included 56,445 women who had an unintended birth between 2012 and 2015 and complete data from the Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS).
finding: Experiencing intimate partner violence and having more psychosocial stressors were independently associated with not using any postpartum contraceptive method.
